t: Section 210(d) of the Energy Policy Act of 2005 (42 U.S.C. 15855(d)) is amended by striking “$50,000,000 for each of the fiscal years 2006 through 2016” and inserting “$50,000,000 for fiscal year 2006 and $35,000,000 for each of fiscal years 2007 through 2016”.

fable.w: This section only amends the dollar amounts authorized to be appropriated under section 210(d) of the Energy Policy Act of 2005. A tempting reading is that the underlying grant program might involve outside parties, but this text itself contains no consultation, comment period, hearing, advisory body, rulemaking, or right to sue. No party outside the federal government is brought into any federal decision.
fable.s: is amended by striking “$50,000,000 for each of the fiscal years 2006 through 2016” and inserting “$50,000,000 for fiscal year 2006 and $35,000,000 for each of fiscal years 2007 through 2016”

opus.w: This section only changes the funding amounts authorized for fiscal years 2007 through 2016. It sets up no consultation, comment period, hearing, advisory body, rulemaking, or right to sue for anyone outside the federal government. The underlying grant program does not count, because grant applications are excluded from participation, and nothing in this text involves outside parties at all.
opus.b: 1. **Tempting reading:** Section 210 of the Energy Policy Act of 2005 sets up a grant program, so you might read this as a decision involving outside parties. That fails because this section only changes the dollar amounts Congress authorizes for certain fiscal years. Nobody outside the federal government is consulted, given a hearing, put on an advisory body, or given a right to sue. And the definition excludes grant applications anyway.

qwen_chat.w: This section is a purely fiscal amendment that adjusts appropriation amounts for specific fiscal years. It does not establish any process for consultation, coordination, or participation with entities outside the federal government. There are no advisory committees, public comment periods, or requirements to consult with states, tribes, or the public mentioned in this text.
qwen_chat.s: Section 210(d) of the Energy Policy Act of 2005 (42 U.S.C. 15855(d)) is amended by striking “$50,000,000 for each of the fiscal years 2006 through 2016” and inserting “$50,000,000 for fiscal year 2006 and $35,000,000 for each of fiscal years 2007 through 2016”.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that changing funding levels affects who can participate in programs, but the text itself contains no procedural requirement for consultation, comment, or coordination with outside parties. It is purely a fiscal amendment.
